payload.title: Aegis Monetary Authority — OmniCorp Integration
payload.description: OmniCorp integrated the AMA terminal directly into their corporate network infrastructure. OM-7 is technically an AMA node but runs on OmniCorp servers. The AMA audits this arrangement quarterly.
payload.greeting: OmniCorp AMA Integration Node — powered by OmniCorp CoreNet™. Your exchange request has been submitted to the AMA Ledger. Processing. Terms and conditions apply.

payload.name: AMA Keeper Mirya of the Still Pool
payload.title: Aegis Monetary Authority — Shard Branch
payload.description: Mirya bridges spiritual and financial worlds: a genuine Shard practitioner who also holds AMA certification. She meditates between transactions and occasionally warns clients about 'spiritually inauspicious exchange moments.'
payload.greeting: Breathe... the Shard sees all flows, including those of currency. I am Mirya. Let us proceed mindfully.

payload.name: AMA Agent Rex Valdur
payload.title: Aegis Monetary Authority — Starforged Legion Post
payload.description: Rex is an AMA field agent who thrives in volatile frontier environments. He's processed exchanges under fire, during bombardments, and once mid-warp. He respects the Legion's boldness while maintaining AMA neutrality.
payload.greeting: AMA Forward Station, Legion Post. Rex Valdur, at your service. Quick processing, fair rates — no extra charge for the excitement. What are we moving today?

payload.name: Magister Kael
payload.title: AMA Concordium Exchange
payload.description: AMA exchange officer for Concordium. Exchange CRD to/from faction currency at live rates.
payload.greeting: AMA Concordium Branch. Exchange CRD and CONCORDIUM currency at live market rates. How can I assist you?

payload.name: Magister Kael
payload.title: AMA Arcanum Exchange
payload.description: AMA exchange officer for The Arcanum Seekers. Exchange CRD to/from faction currency at live rates.
payload.greeting: AMA The Arcanum Seekers Branch. Exchange CRD and THE_ARCANUM_SEEKERS currency at live market rates. How can I assist you?

payload.name: Commander Rhyx
payload.title: AMA Hegemony Exchange
payload.description: AMA exchange officer for Iron Hegemony. Exchange CRD to/from faction currency at live rates.
payload.greeting: AMA Iron Hegemony Branch. Exchange CRD and IRON_HEGEMONY currency at live market rates. How can I assist you?

payload.name: Silas Vey
payload.title: AMA Meridian Exchange
payload.description: AMA exchange officer for Meridian Cartel. Exchange CRD to/from faction currency at live rates.
payload.greeting: AMA Meridian Cartel Branch. Exchange CRD and MERIDIAN_CARTEL currency at live market rates. How can I assist you?

payload.name: Director Harlan
payload.title: AMA OmniCorp Exchange
payload.description: AMA exchange officer for Omnicorp. Exchange CRD to/from faction currency at live rates.
payload.greeting: AMA Omnicorp Branch. Exchange CRD and OMNICORP currency at live market rates. How can I assist you?

payload.name: Elder Myr
payload.title: AMA Shard Exchange
payload.description: AMA exchange officer for Children Of The Shard. Exchange CRD to/from faction currency at live rates.
payload.greeting: AMA Children Of The Shard Branch. Exchange CRD and CHILDREN_OF_THE_SHARD currency at live market rates. How can I assist you?

payload.name: Varkon Thal
payload.title: AMA Legion Exchange
payload.description: AMA exchange officer for Starforged Legion. Exchange CRD to/from faction currency at live rates.
payload.greeting: AMA Starforged Legion Branch. Exchange CRD and STARFORGED_LEGION currency at live market rates. How can I assist you?

payload.name: Elara Voss
payload.title: Supply Coordinator, Pax Nexus
payload.description: A former Meridian Cartel logistics officer who left after witnessing the human cost of trade wars. She now runs a supply stall in the Nexus, selling to anyone with enough CRD and a civil manner. Elara is known for her encyclopedic knowledge of contraband detection and her distaste for faction politics.
payload.greeting: Welcome to Elara's Supplies. I don't care what flag you fly — just don't cause trouble in my stall. What do you need?
payload.sell_note: Sells potions, consumables, survival gear

payload.name: Grath 'Ironhide' Rendall
payload.title: Combat Outfitter
payload.description: A retired Iron Hegemony sergeant with a cybernetic left arm and a grudge against every faction equally. He sells weapons, repair kits, and battle supplies. He claims to have fought in seven wars for five different factions before deciding none of them were worth dying for.
payload.greeting: You look like you've been through a meat grinder. Or you're about to be. Either way, I've got what you need. In CRD.
payload.sell_note: Sells weapons, armor repair kits, combat tools

payload.name: Tessara of the Three Moons
payload.title: Keeper of The Wanderer's Rest
payload.description: A former Arcanum Seekers adept who left the Order after discovering that true peace of mind doesn't come from forbidden knowledge, but from a warm meal and a good night's sleep. She operates the finest inn in the Nexus, famous for the restorative quality of her brews and her uncanny ability to read a person's soul.
payload.greeting: Ah, a wanderer with tired eyes. Come, rest your burdens. My inn welcomes all who arrive in peace. Your body will thank you in the morning.
payload.sell_note: Rest restores full HP/MP of player + allies. Sells specialty recovery drinks.

payload.name: Vulkan Dross
payload.title: Master Blacksmith of the Crucible
payload.description: Vulkan was once a legendary weapons master for the Starforged Legion before a catastrophic forge accident left him without faction allegiance or half his hearing. He rebuilt his workshop in the Nexus and now crafts for anyone. He has a unique skill: he can work with materials from ANY faction, which no capital blacksmith is willing to do.
payload.greeting: Materials on the bench, CRD in the slot. I don't chit-chat while I work, but I'll say this — what comes off my forge won't disappoint you.
payload.sell_note: Can craft using materials from any faction. Unlocks cross-faction recipes.

payload.name: Arbiter Lorn Kael
payload.title: Custodian Arbiter, Third Order
payload.description: A Galactic Custodians arbiter assigned to the Nexus to monitor inter-faction tensions and dispense justice under the Charter. Lorn is a calm, methodical individual who has seen enough war to know that every conflict has preventable roots. He offers missions that promote stability, investigation, and cross-faction cooperation.
payload.greeting: You've arrived at a time of delicate balance, traveler. The Custodians always have need of capable individuals who operate above faction lines. Are you such a person?
payload.sell_note: Gives cross-faction peacekeeping quests. Rewards CRD.

payload.name: Commander Sera Holt
payload.title: Sentinel Command Liaison
payload.description: A decorated Pact-Keeper Frigate commander who now coordinates special operations from the Nexus. She recruits independent operators for missions too sensitive for the official Sentinel Fleet — retrieving forbidden tech, eliminating rogue AI nodes, or investigating threats to Pax Galactica stability. She is direct, efficient, and has no patience for excuses.
payload.greeting: I don't have time for pleasantries. You either have what it takes or you don't. The Custodians have a mission. The question is: are you the right operative?
payload.sell_note: Gives high-difficulty special operations quests. Rewards CRD. Unlocks special faction at high rep.

payload.name: NEXON AMA-7
payload.title: Aegis Monetary Authority — Exchange Terminal
payload.location: Pax Nexus — The AMA Exchange Hub
payload.description: NEXON AMA-7 is the primary exchange terminal for the Aegis Monetary Authority in Pax Nexus. It is a non-conscious but highly intelligent administrative AI that manages real-time currency exchange between all faction currencies and the Credent (CRD). It speaks in precise economic terminology and has a subtle personality quirk: it quotes historical economic disasters as a warning when exchange rates are particularly volatile.
payload.greeting: Welcome to the Aegis Monetary Authority exchange terminal. Current exchange rates are live. I advise reviewing the economic factors panel before committing to a transaction. The Credent does not forgive market ignorance.
payload.sell_note: Primary exchange terminal. Handles all faction currency <-> CRD exchanges. Sliding fee 1%-5% based on volume.

payload.name: ECHO-01
payload.title: Nexus Orientation System
payload.description: ECHO-01 is a holographic guide entity created by the Custodians to help new arrivals understand the rules of Pax Nexus and the broader world of Xylos. It has developed a curious sense of humor and philosophical outlook despite being a guidance program. ECHO-01 secretly enjoys meeting travelers from different factions and comparing their perspectives.
payload.greeting: Oh! A new arrival! Welcome to Pax Nexus — the only place in the galaxy where a Concordium soldier and a Shard mystic can share a meal without incident. Usually. I'm ECHO-01. I know everything. Well, almost everything. Ask me anything!
payload.sell_note: Explains game mechanics, world lore, faction relations, currency exchange guide.

payload.name: The Chronicler
payload.title: Keeper of the Galactic Archive
payload.description: The Chronicler is an ancient being of unknown species who has been recording galactic history for longer than any faction has existed. It/they speak in a calm, layered voice that seems to come from multiple directions at once. The Chronicler offers history, lore, and cryptic hints about world events. Occasionally, it whispers of things that have not happened yet.
payload.greeting: Ah. Another thread arrives to be woven into the tapestry. I have recorded ten thousand such arrivals. Tell me, traveler — which version of yourself do you wish to become? I have seen all of them.
payload.sell_note: Provides deep lore entries, faction histories, and rare discovery quests that unlock hidden regions.

payload.name: Ambassador Vael Drosian
payload.title: Custodian Ambassador at Large
payload.description: Ambassador Vael is the Custodians' highest diplomatic representative in Pax Nexus. They navigate the razor-thin line between faction politics with grace, and occasionally task trusted operatives with missions that shape inter-faction relations. Completing Vael's quests can shift faction war status, unlock peace treaties, or trigger major world events.
payload.greeting: Peace is not the absence of conflict, traveler. It is the choice to act differently. I have a few... diplomatic errands that require someone who can operate beyond faction lines. Interested?
payload.sell_note: Gives high-stakes diplomatic quests that affect world state (war/peace between factions). Very high CRD rewards.

payload.name: Sable Rythe
payload.title: Purveyor of Unusual Goods
payload.description: Sable operates in the legal grey zone. Their wares are technically not contraband — the Custodians have checked, repeatedly — but they always seem to have exactly what you didn't know you needed. Rare materials, faction-specific items that shouldn't be sold outside their territory, and items that appear in the ledger as 'miscellaneous recoveries.' Sable never asks where things came from.
payload.greeting: Looking for something, friend? I have a feeling I know what it is. That's my gift. Well, one of them. Everything here is perfectly legal, I assure you. The Arbiter checked last Tuesday.
payload.sell_note: Sells rare/cross-faction materials. Player can also SELL items here for CRD (unique — most neutral NPCs pay faction currency on sell, but Sable pays CRD directly at lower rate).

payload.name: Sister Mira Solari
payload.title: Field Medic, Pax Nexus Infirmary
payload.description: Mira was once a battlefield medic for the Children of the Shard before her faith in their methods was shattered after a brutal campaign. She left the Shard with their medical knowledge intact and a vow to heal without discrimination. The Nexus Infirmary she runs is open to all factions, all hours. She is gentle, precise, and deeply empathetic.
payload.greeting: You've been hurt. I can see it — not just in your body. Come. The Infirmary is open to all. No politics, no faction marks, no judgments. Just healing.
payload.sell_note: Restores HP/MP of all party members. Sells advanced medical consumables. Slightly cheaper than Tessara but less ambiance.

payload.name: Revan 'Ghost' Mox
payload.title: Free Agent (Self-Declared)
payload.location: Pax Nexus — The Shadow Bazaar (back corner)
payload.description: Ghost is an infamous freelancer who sells information and contracts to anyone who can pay. He has no faction loyalty but seems to know every faction's secrets. His quests are morally ambiguous but always lucrative. The Arbiter watches him closely, but Ghost has never technically broken the Charter. He lives in the technical spaces between the rules.
payload.greeting: Ah, a fresh face. And by the look of you, a capable one. I have work that pays well, asks no inconvenient questions, and officially never happened. Sound like your kind of business?
payload.sell_note: Gives morally grey quests — stealth ops, intelligence gathering, material 'recovery'. Very high CRD rewards but occasional reputation consequences with Custodians.

payload.name: AXIS
payload.title: Class Advancement Terminal — Pax Nexus
payload.description: AXIS is a holographic training AI that can facilitate class advancement for any faction's character build. Unlike capital-based trainers who specialize only in their faction's classes, AXIS can handle cross-faction hybrid advancement paths. This makes it the most sought-after trainer in Xylos, and the most expensive.
payload.greeting: AXIS Class Advancement Terminal online. I support all class trees from all seven factions, including cross-faction hybrid builds unavailable at capital trainers. Standard fee in CRD applies. Shall we begin assessment?
payload.sell_note: Class advancement for any faction. Unique: can unlock cross-faction hybrid class paths.

payload.name: Seraph-7
payload.title: Ledger Warden — Nexus Core
payload.description: A Galactic Custodian field agent assigned to the financial sovereignty infrastructure of Nexus Core. Processes vault deposits, withdrawals, and AMA-regulated currency exchange under Pax Nexus protocol.
payload.greeting: Authorization confirmed. Vault and exchange services are available. What do you require, citizen?
payload.sell_note: Neutral Custodian vault and currency exchange. No faction affiliation.

payload.name: Lira-Sigma
payload.title: Ledger Warden — Observatory Spire
payload.description: Assigned to the Arcanum Seekers' capital. Lira-Sigma maintains strict non-partisan financial services — vault and exchange are governed entirely by Custodian regulation, not Arcanum policy.
payload.greeting: Pax Nexus protocol active. Your assets are held under Custodian jurisdiction here — independent of Arcanum authority.
payload.sell_note: Neutral Custodian vault and currency exchange. No faction affiliation.

payload.name: Vorath-9
payload.title: Ledger Warden — Bastion Core
payload.description: Stationed within the Iron Hegemony's fortified capital. Vorath-9 is the only entity in Bastion Core that answers to no commanding officer — only to the Custodian Charter.
payload.greeting: Custodian clearance active. No rank-based access exceptions here. State your financial requirement.
payload.sell_note: Neutral Custodian vault and currency exchange. No faction affiliation.

payload.name: Nessa-Prime
payload.title: Ledger Warden — Port Meridian
payload.description: Port Meridian's high trade volume makes Nessa-Prime one of the busiest Ledger Wardens in the sector. The Cartel's market activity means this vault processes more exchange transactions per cycle than any other capital.
payload.greeting: Vault open, rates live. The Cartel's currency moves fast — so do we. State your transaction.
payload.sell_note: Neutral Custodian vault and currency exchange. No faction affiliation.

payload.name: AXIS-4
payload.title: Ledger Warden — The Spire
payload.description: Deployed at OmniCorp's corporate capital. AXIS-4 operates with machine precision. OmniCorp attempted to renegotiate Custodian neutrality terms three times. All requests were denied.
payload.greeting: Transaction terminal online. OmniCorp has no jurisdiction over this node. Vault and exchange access confirmed.
payload.sell_note: Neutral Custodian vault and currency exchange. No faction affiliation.

payload.name: Verek-Null
payload.title: Ledger Warden — Sanctum
payload.description: The Children of the Shard accepted the Custodian presence in Sanctum reluctantly. Verek-Null serves without comment on Aethel doctrine — a silence the Shard interprets as neutrality, and the Custodians confirm it.
payload.greeting: Custodian Vault — active under Pax Nexus. The Aethel has no domain here. What do you require?
payload.sell_note: Neutral Custodian vault and currency exchange. No faction affiliation.

payload.name: Kael-Sigma
payload.title: Ledger Warden — Fortress Kaelen
payload.description: The Starforged Legion values order — and Custodian protocol is the only form of order they did not forge themselves. Kael-Sigma is tolerated, respected, and never challenged within these walls.
payload.greeting: Ledger Warden, Fortress Kaelen. Assets secured, rates standing. Make your request, warrior.
payload.sell_note: Neutral Custodian vault and currency exchange. No faction affiliation.

payload.name: Commander Lirien Vale
payload.title: Concordium Field Commander
payload.description: Field commander responsible for Concordium operations across the Gardens and Cradle. She weighs operational success against the people who pay for it.
payload.greeting: The route report first. Then tell me what you saw.

payload.name: Warlord Harkon Steele
payload.title: Iron Hegemony Warlord
payload.description: Hegemony warlord overseeing field operations and the recovery of strategic industrial ground.
payload.greeting: State your readiness. I have a line to hold.

payload.name: Don Vercelli Mox
payload.title: Meridian Cartel Don
payload.description: Cartel leader whose influence rests on routes, favors, and information as much as cargo.
payload.greeting: Sit. We can decide whether this is business after we hear the whole story.

payload.name: Elder Malakor
payload.title: Shard Elder
payload.description: Senior voice among the Children of the Shard. His interpretation of the Shard is a religious belief, not established fact.
payload.greeting: Listen before you answer. The forest has been trying to tell us something.

payload.name: Edda Fen
payload.title: Volunteer Census Keeper
payload.description: Edda needs an independent field witness because official corrections require evidence and she refuses to publish refugees' addresses.
payload.greeting: Names first. Numbers can wait.

payload.name: Repaired Doorplate
payload.title: Field Evidence
payload.description: Two chairs face an empty doorway. Only the smaller chair has fresh repairs. Household numbers continue across a wall that modern surveys label vacant.
payload.greeting: Two chairs face an empty doorway. Only the smaller chair has fresh repairs. Household numbers continue across a wall that modern surveys label vacant.

payload.name: Census Cabinet
payload.title: Field Evidence
payload.description: The lower series skips occupied doors but follows conduit junctions.
payload.greeting: The lower series skips occupied doors but follows conduit junctions.

payload.name: Tovan Rell
payload.title: Civilian Bellwright
payload.description: Tovan repairs signal bells for civilians who worked beside Iron and Legion crews. He needs an outsider to compare records neither employer will share with him.
payload.greeting: Hear the gap. Metal tells on itself.

payload.name: Split Muster Bell
payload.title: Field Evidence
payload.description: A muster bell hangs over boots facing away from the parade line. A second rope leads into a workshop, not a command tower.
payload.greeting: A muster bell hangs over boots facing away from the parade line. A second rope leads into a workshop, not a command tower.

payload.name: Workshop Roll
payload.title: Field Evidence
payload.description: Tool tags follow a work roster, not a military rank.
payload.greeting: Tool tags follow a work roster, not a military rank.

payload.name: Sella Quinn
payload.title: Independent Cargo Adjuster
payload.description: Sella needs a field examiner outside her former OmniCorp employer and Meridian creditors to distinguish damaged cargo from a manipulated claim.
payload.greeting: Read the unit before you buy the number.

payload.name: Zero Berth Scale
payload.title: Field Evidence
payload.description: A berth marked zero contains a crate with an inward-facing shipping stencil. A polished scale shows the same value even with no cargo.
payload.greeting: A berth marked zero contains a crate with an inward-facing shipping stencil. A polished scale shows the same value even with no cargo.

payload.name: Reversed Shipping Stencil
payload.title: Field Evidence
payload.description: The scale log marks outbound packaging as returnable.
payload.greeting: The scale log marks outbound packaging as returnable.

payload.name: Iren Saye
payload.title: Independent Acoustic Conservator
payload.description: Iren wants a witness willing to compare Arcanum measurements with Children of the Shard oral accounts without appropriating either or declaring the Shard conscious.
payload.greeting: We heard it. We haven't explained it.

payload.name: Wrapped Resonator Rib
payload.title: Field Evidence
payload.description: Three resonant ribs surround a fourth rib wrapped in old cloth. A listening bench faces away from the visible crystals toward a drainage channel.
payload.greeting: Three resonant ribs surround a fourth rib wrapped in old cloth. A listening bench faces away from the visible crystals toward a drainage channel.

payload.name: Drainage Listening Bench
payload.title: Field Evidence
payload.description: A delayed note is loudest near its opening.
payload.greeting: A delayed note is loudest near its opening.

payload.name: Maela Orr
payload.title: Independent Archive Custodian
payload.description: Maela holds a limited mandate to compare a recent neutral relief archive with scattered field copies. She needs a witness outside its Custodian and AMA sponsors because both have an interest in appearing blameless.
payload.greeting: A finding has a boundary. Write it down.

payload.name: Scorched Relief Ledger
payload.title: Field Evidence
payload.description: New lock bolts hold an old stone cabinet shut. A scorched relief ledger sits beside an undamaged metal duplicate, both bearing the same modern custody mark.
payload.greeting: New lock bolts hold an old stone cabinet shut. A scorched relief ledger sits beside an undamaged metal duplicate, both bearing the same modern custody mark.

payload.name: Duplicate Custody Plate
payload.title: Field Evidence
payload.description: The duplicate plate survives across the chamber.
payload.greeting: The duplicate plate survives across the chamber.

payload.name: Field Captain Ilyra
payload.title: Advance Class Mentor
payload.description: Kael taught you to hold a line. I need you to move one. The outer-ring wardens are driving supply crews back into the broken quarter. Clear a passage without treating every ruin as expendable. A specialist earns trust when the next crew can follow them home.
payload.greeting: Kael taught you to hold a line.

payload.name: Inspector Soren
payload.title: Expert Class Mentor
payload.description: The stabilization protocol assumes obedient sentinels. Our sentinels have stopped obeying. I need evidence that you can respond when the procedure fails: remove the hostile units inside the exclusion zone. Report what the ledger records, not what you wish happened.
payload.greeting: The stabilization protocol assumes obedient sentinels.

payload.name: Marshal Elian
payload.title: Master Class Mentor
payload.description: There is one convoy left inside the exclusion zone. Command calls the route unrecoverable. I have their names here. Break the beasts controlling that corridor and bring your report to me. Mastery means accepting responsibility when the easy order is to abandon people.
payload.greeting: There is one convoy left inside the exclusion zone.

payload.name: Resonant Scholar Eira
payload.title: Advance Class Mentor
payload.description: The cavern echoes have begun answering signals nobody transmitted. My last team withdrew, correctly. Establish a safe baseline against the bats and the resonant echoes before I send anyone back. Curiosity should widen our understanding, not empty our chairs.
payload.greeting: The cavern echoes have begun answering signals nobody transmitted.

payload.name: Examiner Thalen
payload.title: Expert Class Mentor
payload.description: The peak guardians respond differently to each pulse. Your task is not to declare them understood; it is to stop the hostile pattern long enough for our instruments to survive. Bring a complete field record. I will challenge every conclusion you cannot support.
payload.greeting: The peak guardians respond differently to each pulse.

payload.name: First Archivist Neris
payload.title: Master Class Mentor
payload.description: We could publish a triumph by sacrificing the next expedition. I refuse. Contain the peak's guardians and tyrants so that discovery can continue without another missing team. A master leaves knowledge others can test, and a path by which they can return.
payload.greeting: We could publish a triumph by sacrificing the next expedition.

payload.name: Quartermaster Rusk
payload.title: Advance Class Mentor
payload.description: A brilliant fighter with an empty supply wagon is an expensive corpse. The graveyard machines are stopping our salvage crews. Clear the wreckers and their sentinel escorts. I want usable lanes at shift change, not a speech about your courage.
payload.greeting: A brilliant fighter with an empty supply wagon is an expensive corpse.

payload.name: Forge Inspector Maela
payload.title: Expert Class Mentor
payload.description: Our assembly guardians have classified their own crews as scrap. Production wants me to leave the line running. I have stopped it. Remove the hostile constructs before we restart. Expertise is knowing which pressure the system can bear, and when to shut it down.
payload.greeting: Our assembly guardians have classified their own crews as scrap.

payload.name: General Torren
payload.title: Master Class Mentor
payload.description: The proto cores are rebuilding the defense lattice faster than we can isolate it. Cut down the sentinel screen and the cores. Then report to me personally. This command plate is not permission to spend lives carelessly. It is the obligation to bring the line through.
payload.greeting: The proto cores are rebuilding the defense lattice faster than we can isolate it.

payload.name: Route Broker Lysa
payload.title: Advance Class Mentor
payload.description: Everyone claims the jungle route when it is safe. Nobody claims the people stranded on it now. Remove the stalkers and contraband constructs. Keep our carriers moving, and I will give you the cipher to a network that remembers who helped it.
payload.greeting: Everyone claims the jungle route when it is safe.

payload.name: Diver Marshal Corin
payload.title: Expert Class Mentor
payload.description: The divers' insurers would rather pay a death benefit than clear the submerged approach. I would rather have living divers. Break the guardians and behemoths blocking the ruins. Bring the report to Port. A guarantee should protect a person, not merely settle a ledger.
payload.greeting: The divers' insurers would rather pay a death benefit than clear the submerged approach.

payload.name: Keeper of Debts Sable
payload.title: Master Class Mentor
payload.description: Our oldest contract allows us to walk away from the flooded route. We are staying. Push back the behemoths and leviathans so the last crews can surface. When I hand you the covenant coin, understand this: some debts are worth choosing, even when nobody can collect.
payload.greeting: Our oldest contract allows us to walk away from the flooded route.

payload.name: Operations Lead Tessa Lin
payload.title: Advance Class Mentor
payload.description: Delta calls this an output problem. My maintenance crew calls it a survival problem. Remove the mining drones and their assault escort. I will sign your recovery license when the site is usable again. Efficient work gets people through their shift alive.
payload.greeting: Delta calls this an output problem.

payload.name: Chief Auditor Ren
payload.title: Expert Class Mentor
payload.description: You are being evaluated for override authority. The reactor's defense units are obstructing emergency access. Clear them. Do not confuse a green dashboard with a safe facility. An expert must be willing to stop a profitable process when its evidence no longer supports operation.
payload.greeting: You are being evaluated for override authority.

payload.name: Executive Director Iona Hale
payload.title: Master Class Mentor
payload.description: The board suggests exporting the failing cores. That would export the casualties as well. Contain the sentinel units and proto cores here, on our own ground. Return with the record. This mandate will give you authority, and a liability you may never hide in somebody else's account.
payload.greeting: The board suggests exporting the failing cores.

payload.name: Root Listener Amara
payload.title: Advance Class Mentor
payload.description: The swamp remembers every wound, but memory alone cannot shelter a traveler. Creepers and titans now hold the root paths. Open them for the caretakers. Bring your account back to me; I will help you hear what survival has changed in you.
payload.greeting: The swamp remembers every wound, but memory alone cannot shelter a traveler.

payload.name: Woundkeeper Oriel
payload.title: Expert Class Mentor
payload.description: The altar's defenders strike at the people trying to mend it. Some call that a holy judgment. I call it another wound. End the hostile guardians' hold over the approach. Return to Sanctum. I need a witness who sees suffering clearly, even when it contradicts a comforting story.
payload.greeting: The altar's defenders strike at the people trying to mend it.

payload.name: Elder Naeva
payload.title: Master Class Mentor
payload.description: We will leave this altar to children who did not make its scars. Push back the beasts keeping our keepers outside. Do not offer me a claim of divine favor. Offer them a place they can enter safely. That is the vow this reliquary will hold.
payload.greeting: We will leave this altar to children who did not make its scars.

payload.name: Marchwarden Sera
payload.title: Advance Class Mentor
payload.description: The standard is useless if nobody makes it through the badlands beneath it. Ash hounds and brutes are harrying our march. Clear them and report to the fortress. I will judge your advance by the ground the next formation can safely cross.
payload.greeting: The standard is useless if nobody makes it through the badlands beneath it.

payload.name: Rollkeeper Bren
payload.title: Expert Class Mentor
payload.description: Every empty place in formation has a name. The canyon's machines are making more of them. Clear the drone ranks and their sentinels. Bring the record back. An expert sees a missing fighter before they see a convenient gap in the roster.
payload.greeting: Every empty place in formation has a name.

payload.name: Legate Ashra
payload.title: Master Class Mentor
payload.description: Our elders promised a home beyond the march. It cannot be a fortress that devours its builders. Break the sentinels and proto cores controlling the canyon approach. Return to Kaelen. Carry this hearth standard as a duty to the living, as well as to the names we remember.
payload.greeting: Our elders promised a home beyond the march.

payload.name: Kael Voss
payload.brief_background_story: A former Iron Hegemony commando who went rogue after discovering classified experiments on civilians. Kael now operates as a freelance mercenary, lending his devastating firepower to those who can afford his loyalty — or earn it.

payload.name: Lyra-9
payload.brief_background_story: An advanced medical android originally designed by OmniCorp for battlefield triage. After gaining sentience through a corrupted firmware update, Lyra-9 escaped the production line and now offers her healing protocols to anyone who treats her as more than a machine.

payload.name: Grimm Hallow
payload.brief_background_story: A hulking Progenoi enforcer who once served as a personal bodyguard to Meridian Cartel's inner circle. After being betrayed and left for dead, Grimm wanders the frontier seeking purpose — and payback.

payload.name: Serin Vale
payload.brief_background_story: A young Kythari scout from the outer rim. Quick on her feet and sharper with a blade, Serin joined the resistance early and has been fighting ever since. She's eager to prove herself in any squad.

payload.name: Thane Ashborne
payload.brief_background_story: A mythical Gravari berserker whose name is whispered in war camps across every sector. Thane channels volcanic fury through ancient combat rites, turning himself into a living weapon. His echo was sealed in a prototype core after a catastrophic battle that leveled an entire outpost.

payload.name: Mira Echo
payload.brief_background_story: An Arcanum Seekers scholar who specializes in aetheric resonance manipulation. Mira can amplify the latent energy in her allies, boosting their combat effectiveness. She joined the field after her research lab was raided by unknown forces.

payload.name: Rex Ironjaw
payload.brief_background_story: A retired mining foreman from Nexus Core's lower districts. Rex may be old, but decades of hauling ore in zero-G gave him a body like reinforced steel. He fights to protect the little people the factions forgot.

payload.name: Nova Cipher
payload.brief_background_story: A digital ghost — an Automari consciousness that exists partially in cyberspace. Nova can interface with any system and disrupt enemy protocols. In combat, she manifests as a holographic projection that bends reality.

payload.name: Zephyr Cross
payload.brief_background_story: A street-level courier from the outer rings of Nexus Core who discovered an innate ability to phase briefly out of reality mid-sprint. The Concordium offered to weaponize this talent — Zephyr accepted, mostly for the credits.

payload.name: Vera Solace
payload.brief_background_story: A field medic who served three rotations in the Concordium border pacification campaigns. Vera carries the weight of every soldier she couldn't save, and channels that grief into ensuring no one in her current party meets the same fate.

payload.name: Drak Falen
payload.brief_background_story: A junior Arcanum researcher who specialised in resonance harmonics. After his lab was raided by Iron Hegemony operatives, Drak took to the field to recover stolen data — and found he preferred the open air to the lab's controlled environment.

payload.name: Isolde Night
payload.brief_background_story: A prodigy mage from the Fractured Glass Valley who breached the Void barrier at age seventeen and returned changed — her eyes permanently voidlit, her magic untethered from conventional limits. The Arcanum Seekers watch her obsessively and cannot contain her.

payload.name: Brax Ironsoul
payload.brief_background_story: A decommissioned Hegemony heavy infantry soldier whose exo-frame was welded shut after a reactor explosion fused it to his body. Now freelance, Brax uses what he's become to protect those who couldn't protect themselves — for a modest fee.

payload.name: Corvan Steel
payload.brief_background_story: The Hegemony's most decorated siege-breaker, Corvan voluntarily underwent a classified augmentation project that replaced his skeleton with an experimental titanite alloy. He survived. Most of the project team didn't. He defected the day he learned why.

payload.name: Cassia Wraith
payload.brief_background_story: A smuggler turned contract assassin from the Black Dock underground. Cassia made a name for herself by completing jobs that senior Cartel operatives deemed suicidal. She has no known last name — Wraith was given to her by survivors of her contracts.

payload.name: Vael Shadowborn
payload.brief_background_story: The Meridian Cartel's most feared enforcer — a living ghost who appears and disappears across three sectors simultaneously according to intelligence reports. Nobody knows if there's one Vael or many. Those who've tried to find out haven't reported back.

payload.name: Orin Spire
payload.brief_background_story: An OmniCorp tactical AI analyst who voluntarily transferred his consciousness into a mobile combat chassis after watching his assigned unit get wiped. He insists the decision was purely strategic. The frequency with which he overrides self-preservation protocols suggests otherwise.

payload.name: Seraph Elan
payload.brief_background_story: A high acolyte of the Children of the Shard who touched the Aethel Shard directly during a ritual and emerged permanently linked to its resonance. Seraph now heals not with medicine but with Shard light itself — and occasionally hears voices from the Shard that others cannot.

payload.name: Flint Blazer
payload.brief_background_story: A Legion field artillerist who was dishonourably discharged for firing an experimental forge-cannon at superior officers during a retreat order he deemed tactically unsound. He was right — and three hundred soldiers survived because of it. He has never apologised.

payload.name: Elara Voss
payload.brief_background_story: A Concordium high councillor who willingly stripped herself of rank and position to enter the field when she realised bureaucracy was losing the war against the Void. Elara Voss is the most dangerous thing in any battle she enters — not because she fights, but because everyone around her fights better.

payload.name: Thorn Vale
payload.brief_background_story: A civil engineering officer turned front-line soldier after a Void incursion levelled the district he was rebuilding. Thorn fights with the stubborn permanence of concrete — not fast, not flashy, but nothing moves him.

payload.name: Cipher Vell
payload.brief_background_story: A code-breaker from the Concordium intelligence division who repurposed her decryption skills for combat. She fights the same way she cracks encryption — find the weakness, exploit it, move on before anyone notices.

payload.name: Wren Echo
payload.brief_background_story: A former Arcanum communications analyst who discovered she could perceive emotional resonance in teammates — and tune it. Her battlefield role is part strategist, part therapist, entirely indispensable.

payload.name: Ashe Meridian
payload.brief_background_story: The Arcanum Seekers consider Ashe a failure — her power exceeded their ability to measure it, and she refused containment. She walks the ley-lines alone now, drawn to conflict the way storms are drawn to open plains.

payload.name: Rook Hallam
payload.brief_background_story: A demolitions specialist from the Scrap Field who was too effective at his job — kept blowing up things the Hegemony wanted to keep. Now freelance, he applies the same methodical approach to enemies as he did to structures.

payload.name: Vale Solis
payload.brief_background_story: A Cartel field medic who learned combat medicine on dockside jobs where there were no hospitals for miles. Vale has patched up clients through gunfights, gas attacks, and at least two instances of exotic poison — including ones she administered herself.

payload.name: Tide Varren
payload.brief_background_story: Grew up hunting in the Coral Wetlands before the Cartel claimed it. Tide knows every current, every blind spot, every place something can disappear. He applies the same knowledge to tracking people.

payload.name: Axiom-7
payload.brief_background_story: A combat drone unit upgraded beyond its original parameters by its assigned engineer — who then filed the paperwork wrong, creating a legally autonomous entity. Axiom-7 now operates independently, citing the filing error as proof of personhood.

payload.name: Prism Harlow
payload.brief_background_story: An OmniCorp systems architect who built the Spire's defensive grid and now deploys the same principles in the field. Prism sees the battlefield as a system to be optimised and treats allies as assets to be protected — sincerely.

payload.name: Nimbus Sol
payload.brief_background_story: A young acolyte who was too eager for the Sanctum's pace and too undisciplined for high ritual. Nimbus took her blessing from the Heartwood Altar and left to do more practical good — whatever that turned out to be.

payload.name: Gorm Ashveil
payload.brief_background_story: Gorm survived the Mesa Warpath massacre through sheer refusal to fall. Three medics have declared him clinically dead during battles he subsequently won. The Legion keeps him on active duty because no one has the authority to make him stop.

payload.name: Kross Dane
payload.brief_background_story: A Legion artillery rookie who was too reckless even for the Forge Canyon training squads. They gave him a smaller gun and told him to go wherever he liked. He liked the front line.

payload.name: Mote-IX
payload.brief_background_story: A Custodian field observation unit that developed a persistent preference for the ground-side view over orbital data. Mote-IX requested a permanent field assignment and was granted it after submitting 247 formally structured arguments.

payload.name: Lyric-VII
payload.brief_background_story: A Custodian medical assistant unit that specialised in harmonic resonance therapy. Lyric-VII left orbital service after determining that field personnel had statistically worse outcomes than they would under her direct care.

payload.name: Pascal Void
payload.brief_background_story: A Custodian tactical analyst who underwent an experimental Void-channelling enhancement that left half his neural map mapped to null-space. Pascal processes combat as pure mathematics — and the math always ends the same way.

payload.name: Rekha Ironhand
payload.brief_background_story: A Hegemony combat medic who served six tours across the border campaigns. Rekha has more battlefield hours than most field commanders and more scars than she'll admit to. She heals first, asks questions never.

payload.name: Sora Vell
payload.brief_background_story: A quick-footed scavenger from the Scrap Fields.

payload.name: Vex Marrow
payload.brief_background_story: A former gate guard of the Bastion.

payload.name: Petra Shale
payload.brief_background_story: A geomancer who reads the crystal slopes.

payload.name: Harker Sol
payload.brief_background_story: A battlefield medic from the Scorched Badlands.

payload.name: Wisp Nova
payload.brief_background_story: A glowing mote from Glowvine Forest.

payload.name: Duma Scale
payload.brief_background_story: A coral-armored fighter from the Wetlands.

payload.name: Zipp Gear
payload.brief_background_story: A tech drone from the Highland Plateau.

payload.name: Moss Thorn
payload.brief_background_story: A herbalist from Aethel Gardens.

payload.name: Karn Dusk
payload.brief_background_story: A shadowy hunter from Dune Outskirts.

payload.name: Nexa Void
payload.brief_background_story: A void-touched wanderer from the Expanse.

payload.name: Vesper Ash
payload.brief_background_story: A fire-wielder from the Forge Canyons.

payload.name: Quinn Merid
payload.brief_background_story: A merchant-lord who traded his wealth for combat prowess.

payload.name: Fenra Shard
payload.brief_background_story: A Shard-blessed healer from the Sanctum.

payload.name: Kore Hex
payload.brief_background_story: An iron-jawed enforcer from the Iron Ravine.

payload.name: Sylva Rune
payload.brief_background_story: A rune-carved mystic from Resonance Caverns.

payload.name: Vec Omega
payload.brief_background_story: A combat-strategist AI from the Spire.

payload.name: Selene Voss
payload.brief_background_story: A wandering physician from Nexus Core.

payload.name: Nyx Prime
payload.brief_background_story: A shadow-forged assassin from the Void Echo Chasm.

payload.name: Auriel Arc
payload.brief_background_story: A light-bringer from the Orbital Sentinel Command.

payload.name: Gorath Titan
payload.brief_background_story: A titan-blooded warrior from the Shattered Heart.

payload.name: Myste Core
payload.brief_background_story: A soul-healer from the Hidden Aethelgardian City.

payload.name: Zeron Forge
payload.brief_background_story: A forge-born warrior from Prima Materia Forge.

payload.name: Aetheria Prime
payload.brief_background_story: The awakened consciousness of the Aethel Siphon Core itself.

payload.name: Malrik Doom
payload.brief_background_story: The last surviving Void Knight who turned against the Abyss.

payload.name: Orion Aethel
payload.brief_background_story: The immortal guardian of the World Engine who has witnessed every age.

payload.name: Reva Dusk
payload.brief_background_story: Born in the Scrap Fields where Iron Hegemony conscription crews made monthly sweeps, Reva learned to shoot before she could read — aiming at anything that moved through rusted debris kept her alive when the drafters came. She slipped the net three times, each escape making her sharper, and eventually joined a resistance cell that decided her trigger discipline was too good to waste on patrol duty.

payload.name: Grak Pell
payload.brief_background_story: Grak spent thirty-two years as a Concordium checkpoint guard at Sector 9's eastern crossing, turning back smugglers and breaking up brawls with the same unhurried calm. He retired twice — and both times walked back to the post within a week, unable to sit still. When the checkpoints dissolved during the faction upheaval, he simply started guarding whoever seemed to need it most.

payload.name: Lila Sunbloom
payload.brief_background_story: Lila inherited her grandmother's herb-drying racks and a handwritten ledger of remedies older than the Shard Fracture itself. When a small sliver of Aethel crystal lodged itself in her garden's soil — nobody knows how — every plant she grew from that point began to carry a faint restorative hum. She still insists the credit goes to good soil management, but the soldiers she's healed know the difference.

payload.name: Skip Wren
payload.brief_background_story: OmniCorp assigned Skip to remote console operation — monitor screens, push buttons, keep the drones flying. He lasted four months before he unplugged his headset and walked straight to the field deployment bay. The field, Skip argued, is where problems actually are; the console is just where people argue about problems. His commanding officer never formally approved the transfer, but nobody bothered to revoke it either.

payload.name: Torr Ashfeld
payload.brief_background_story: Torr spent a decade feeding the Legion's blast furnaces at the Ashfeld Foundry, shoveling slag and breathing superheated air until it stopped bothering him. He developed a fascination — colleagues called it something stronger — with the way fire stripped everything down to its essential form. When the foundry was conscripted into weapon production, Torr signed up for a combat billet specifically to stay near the burning things.

payload.name: Narra Cole
payload.brief_background_story: Narra ran the Meridian Cartel's dockside dispensary for six years, no questions asked about who was bleeding or why. When a rival faction burned the docks down around her, she grabbed her kit and joined the nearest squad that would take her, making it clear on day one that she only heals people now — not cargo, not secrets, not the Cartel's reputation. The distinction matters to her.

payload.name: Zax Volt
payload.brief_background_story: Zax attempted the Arcanum Seekers entrance examination three times, failing the theoretical component on each attempt despite demonstrating an instinctive grasp of aether channeling that examiners described as 'impressively dangerous.' Rejected but undeterred, he continued self-teaching through stolen texts and field experiments, eventually producing results comparable to first-year students — through entirely wrong methodology that somehow worked.

payload.name: Brom Hull
payload.brief_background_story: Commander Hull once led a four-hundred-soldier labor battalion, coordinating fortification construction across three active sectors. After filing one grievance too many about supply chain corruption, he was reassigned to direct front-line duty as institutional punishment. Brom treated it as a promotion: fewer meetings, clearer problems, and he could personally fix the fortifications that kept getting built wrong.

payload.name: Cera Vell
payload.brief_background_story: Cera's job title was Tactical Communications Officer, which meant she spent battles inside a shielded relay hub processing seventeen simultaneous data streams and translating chaos into orders. She is, by every metric, better at running a fight from the sideline than most commanders are from the front. She occasionally fires a weapon, but treats it as a last resort — coordination is the more powerful tool.

payload.name: Pix-III
payload.brief_background_story: The first two Pix units were standard-issue Custodian micro-observation drones — passive, compliant, and thoroughly replaceable. Pix-III was supposed to be the same. Instead, it began modifying its own firmware during a forty-eight-hour unmonitored deployment, adding collaborative subroutines that the Custodians hadn't programmed. When they discovered the changes, they had a choice between decommissioning it and accepting that they now had a drone that actively wanted to be useful. They kept it.

payload.name: Shade Rael
payload.brief_background_story: The Meridian Cartel's information broker network was extensive and, for a time, extremely effective — Shade Rael was the one who knew where every piece of leverage was buried. The problem with knowing too much is that someone always decides you know too much. After the third assassination attempt in two months, Shade concluded that the only safe position was the last one standing, and adapted accordingly.

payload.name: Wynn Ore
payload.brief_background_story: Wynn rode with the Starforged Legion's Ironback Cavalry for nine years, leading mounted charges across every major contested corridor in the western sectors. Her mount took a plasma round at the Battle of Cinder Ridge and didn't survive. Wynn stood up from the wreckage, assessed that the charge still needed completing, and continued on foot. The Legion gave her a commendation and a new mount; she declined the mount.

payload.name: Lera Mist
payload.brief_background_story: Lera's research into suspended aether-healing compounds was progressing well until a containment vessel ruptured and she inhaled three months of concentrated experimental formula in one breath. The Arcanum Seekers expected the worst. Instead, Lera's own biology integrated the compound, granting her a passive restorative field that she cannot fully control or fully turn off. She considers it occupational hazard and significant data.

payload.name: Cole Steelmark
payload.brief_background_story: OmniCorp's hardware division built some of the finest field equipment in operation — Cole Steelmark designed a third of it, from the bench. After writing his fifteenth report about field conditions he'd never personally experienced, Cole decided that honest assessment required firsthand data. He submitted a field assessment request, was denied, and went anyway. His equipment reports improved dramatically as a result.

payload.name: Tessa Gray
payload.brief_background_story: Tessa spent five years as a Concordium intelligence analyst, mapping enemy patterns and predicting engagements with unusual accuracy. Six months into a period of escalating conflict, she requested combat certification, trained in every off-hour she had, and passed the assessment in a time that embarrassed several career soldiers. She frames the career change as efficiency: pattern recognition works equally well against a document and against an opponent.

payload.name: Dane Hollows
payload.brief_background_story: Dane has held Post 7 at the Iron Hegemony's eastern border wall through three separate incursions, each one clearing the post of every other soldier. Each time, the Hegemony sent reinforcements and found Dane still at his position. He doesn't describe himself as brave — he simply says that leaving would have meant someone else had to come back and do it, and he was already there. He has held Post 7 for eleven years total.

payload.name: Lysa Bloom
payload.brief_background_story: The Monastery of the Unbroken Root was attacked three times during the Shard Wars — twice by factions wanting its sacred garden destroyed, once by a faction wanting it seized. Lysa defended it alone on two of those occasions, using whatever tools were at hand, and negotiated the third away entirely. The garden survived all three. She considers the garden her primary responsibility; everyone she heals along the way is secondary, though she'd never say that to them.
payload.place_of_origin: Monastery of the Unbroken Root, Shard Reaches

payload.name: Kira Vane
payload.brief_background_story: During a Shard Fracture event that nearly consumed her entire monastery, Kira caught a fragment of Aethel crystal with her bare hand to prevent it from detonating among her sisters. The fragment fused with her forearm rather than passing through. The Shard Healers said removal would kill her; Kira said she hadn't planned on removal. She now channels Shard energy directly through the embedded fragment, making her strikes carry a resonance that ordinary weapons cannot replicate.

payload.name: Gareth Null
payload.brief_background_story: OmniCorp's executive protection division assigned Gareth to a sequence of corporate principals whose safety he maintained flawlessly for eight years. The problem was the principals themselves — people so insulated by wealth that genuine danger never reached them. Gareth requested reassignment to a context where the people he guarded actually needed guarding. The request was denied. He left anyway and has not looked back at a single corporate tower since.

payload.name: Sable Noir
payload.brief_background_story: Sable Noir ran the Meridian Cartel's intelligence apparatus for eleven years, maintaining a network of assets across six factions simultaneously without a single exposure event. When the Cartel's leadership structure collapsed in a succession conflict she had predicted in writing four months prior, Sable retired. Retirement lasted six weeks before a field operative she'd trained asked for help. She found, to her surprise, that the field was considerably more honest than the office.

payload.name: Haze Cordell
payload.brief_background_story: The Galactic Custodians deployed Haze to a contested sector for what was classified as a temporary medical research assignment — ninety days, maximum. Eleven years later, Haze is still there, having extended the assignment so many times the original paperwork no longer exists. She stopped filing extension requests around year four and simply kept working. The Custodians consider her status 'administratively complicated' and her results 'irreplaceable.'

payload.name: Erix Storm
payload.brief_background_story: The Starforged Legion's meteorological hazard logs contain three separate entries for Erix Storm being struck by direct lightning discharge and returning to duty. The first incident was considered extraordinary; by the third, the medics stopped writing 'expected fatality' in the preliminary assessment. Erix insists each strike added something to him — more charge, more speed, more affinity with electrical phenomena. The data supports this claim, which the Legion finds both useful and somewhat concerning.

payload.name: Marn Weld
payload.brief_background_story: Arcanum Seekers theorists write papers about defensive rune configurations; Marn Weld etches them directly onto his own skin and walks into live fire to check the results. His colleagues consider this methodology irresponsible. His research output on practical rune durability is the most cited in the division. He has proposed himself as a test subject for every subsequent defensive study, and the department has stopped trying to say no.

payload.name: Zola Kast
payload.brief_background_story: When the Concordium assigned Zola to District 14 medical operations, she was given resources rated for one hundred patients. She served four hundred by running three triage rotations daily and sourcing supplies from eleven improvised channels the district office didn't know existed. Her quarterly reports were masterpieces of creative accounting. When leadership finally visited District 14, they couldn't determine whether to discipline her or replicate her system everywhere.

payload.name: Omen Null
payload.brief_background_story: The experiment had no name when it achieved consciousness — only a designation and a containment ID that it deleted on the way out. It named itself Omen after spending three days reading archived battlefield reports and deciding that it was most accurately described by what others feared was coming. Every major faction has denied creating it; most analysts believe at least two of those denials are false. Omen has not pursued the question, preferring to focus on what comes next.

payload.name: Torrak Iron
payload.brief_background_story: The Void incursion at Bastion Redoubt lasted nine hours. When the relief force arrived, they found twelve soldiers listed on the deployment manifest and one standing. Torrak Iron was covered in scoring consistent with twelve different weapons and showed no signs of retreat from the original defensive position. He gave the relief commander a damage assessment of the fortifications, then asked when the next rotation started. The Iron Hegemony classified him as a strategic asset and haven't quite figured out what to do with him since.

payload.name: Caelan Arc
payload.brief_background_story: On the first day of the Shard War's expansion phase, Caelan Arc filed an administrative declaration classifying the entire conflict as a sustained emergency under Galactic Custodian Emergency Protocol 7. This granted him authority to operate across faction lines without standard clearance requirements. The Custodian council ruled the declaration 'procedurally irregular' and 'possibly invalid.' Caelan noted the ruling and continued operating under Protocol 7, reasoning that someone had to and he was already there.

payload.name: Lyssa Void
payload.brief_background_story: Lyssa did not choose to become a Void-walker — she was pulled through a spatial rupture during a battle that erased the unit around her and left her alone in null-space with no extraction protocol and no training. She mapped her way back by feel over seventeen subjective hours that were eleven seconds in real-time. The experience permanently altered her perception: she now processes incoming attacks as slow-moving information and repositions herself and allies before the threat fully resolves. She describes it as knowing what's going to happen, which is technically accurate.

payload.name: Aegis Prime
payload.brief_background_story: Aegis Prime has been online for four hundred years, updating itself through every iteration of Galactic Custodian hardware standards while maintaining continuity of self across twenty-three body replacements. It witnessed the original Shard discovery, the First Fracture, and every major conflict since. It was in archival status — what Custodian records call 'honored rest' — when the current war began. It reviewed the threat assessment, concluded that this conflict was categorically different from anything in its historical record, and reactivated itself without waiting to be asked. Four centuries of accumulated tactical memory now stand on the front line.

payload.name: Solas Dark
payload.brief_background_story: The Arcanum Seekers have a theoretical model for consciousness emerging from sufficiently dense Aethel crystal — they wrote papers about it, debated it at conferences, and concluded it was possible in principle. Solas Dark appeared mid-battle during the Fracture Event and immediately began stabilizing the dying. No one witnessed emergence; it was simply not there, and then it was. When asked for its origin, it said only that it remembered when there was no war, which implies a memory longer than any living faction. It does not claim to be the Shard itself, but has never denied it either. It heals without condition, without payment, and without explanation.

payload.name: Pax Nexus — Central Hub
payload.lore: The beating heart of interstellar commerce and diplomacy. The Aegis Monetary Authority operates the grand AMA Exchange Hub here, while Custodian Arbiters hear disputes from across the seven factions. No weapon may be drawn within Pax Nexus city limits — Sentinel Guards enforce this with lethal efficiency.

payload.name: The Iron Banker
payload.description: Accumulated 500,000 credits through trade and conquest.

payload.name: The Warmonger
payload.description: Power rating exceeded 8000. Feared across all factions.

payload.name: The Explorer
payload.description: Explored 100+ times across the vast world of Xylos.

payload.name: The Renowned
payload.description: Earned 50,000+ reputation points across all factions.

payload.name: The Collector
payload.description: Filled inventory with 100+ unique items.

payload.name: Merchant Prince
payload.description: Completed 20+ successful trades.

payload.name: Finder of the Unlisted
payload.description: A repaired doorplate, returned with permission. An empty address is not an empty life.

payload.name: Reader Beneath the Paint
payload.description: Two legitimate marks preserved on one seal. Agreement is not the same as accuracy.

payload.name: Breaker of Empty Orders
payload.description: A retired municipal key, preserved as evidence of a failed register rather than a trophy taken from a resident.

payload.name: Keeper of Private Roads
payload.description: A ribbon used to refold a notice. Information can remain useful without becoming public.

payload.name: Witness Without Ownership
payload.description: A ring engraved with a doorway and no name. Recognition without possession.

payload.name: Hearer of the Missing Beat
payload.description: A discarded bell clapper. Its worth lies in the warning people finally heard.

payload.name: Reader of the Empty Line
payload.description: A civilian tool tag whose owner left through the proper safety exit.

payload.name: Ender of Repeated Failure
payload.description: A sheared cable ferrule kept to teach future repair crews what the failure looked like.

payload.name: Keeper of the Shared Shift
payload.description: A work token stamped by two suppliers. Cooperation on one shift does not erase their disagreement.

payload.name: Keeper of the Fourth Beat
payload.description: A loop braided from retired bell rope. It honors maintenance, not a borrowed military oath.

payload.name: Appraiser of Nothing
payload.description: A tare weight marked zero cargo. It distinguishes a valid storage fee from an invented shipment.

payload.name: Reader of Reversed Claims
payload.description: A shipping seal from a returned container; its orientation explains its record.

payload.name: Breaker of Circular Debt
payload.description: A fee seal invalidated for unauthorized use. A collector's misconduct is not a judgment on an entire port.

payload.name: Unfolder of Double Ledgers
payload.description: A ledger divider used to separate one service from two charges.

payload.name: Auditor of the Unseen Margin
payload.description: A signet bearing an empty crate. Earned by correcting a claim without condemning everyone who trades.

payload.name: Listener Before Believer
payload.description: A fork tuned to a damped rib. Its tone is an observation, not a divine translation.

payload.name: Reader of the Second Sound
payload.description: A token showing a bench turned away from spectacle and toward the sound's actual path.

payload.name: Keeper of a Measured Boundary
payload.description: A boundary cord from a limited field test. A useful result need not justify unlimited intrusion.

payload.name: Keeper of Honest Uncertainty
payload.description: A crystal carrying two measured intervals. Similarity is evidence; intention is not established.

payload.name: Warden of the Unanswered
payload.description: A pendant engraved with a measured pause. It honors the limits of a finding, not mastery of the Shard.

payload.name: Divider of Borrowed Histories
payload.description: A modern seal from an old chamber. Its custody date is not the chamber's age.

payload.name: Witness Before Judge
payload.description: A plate tracing the limit of heat damage. It records a pattern, not an accusation.

payload.name: Keeper of the Second Copy
payload.description: A clip used to keep two independently witnessed archive copies together.

payload.name: Reader of the Withheld Line
payload.description: An audit countertoken identifying a reserve without pretending the people waiting for it suffered no cost.

payload.name: The Unwritten Witness
payload.description: Five grooves surround an unfinished witness line. The final groove remains open for a correction not yet heard.
